Publication tables of models and auxiliary results

lm_table.Rd

lm_table() formats results as a table in plain text (UTF-8 rules), GitHub markdown, LaTeX (booktabs) or HTML, in the spirit of stargazer or gtsummary but without dependencies.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'lm_bvr'
lm_table(
  x,
  ...,
  format = c("text", "markdown", "latex", "html"),
  digits = 3,
  file = NULL,
  title = NULL,
  notes = NULL,
  label = NULL
)

lm_table(x, ...)

# Default S3 method
lm_table(x, ...)

# S3 method for class 'lm_tab'
lm_table(
  x,
  ...,
  format = c("text", "markdown", "latex", "html"),
  file = NULL,
  label = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'data.frame'
lm_table(
  x,
  ...,
  format = c("text", "markdown", "latex", "html"),
  digits = 3,
  file = NULL,
  title = NULL,
  notes = NULL,
  label = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'latentmix'
lm_table(

  ...,
  what = c("fit", "parameters", "classes", "regression"),

Arguments

x

A fitted latentmix model, a list of models, an auxiliary result, a data frame or an lm_tab.

...

For a model: more fitted models (fit comparison; arguments may be named to label the rows). For a bch() result: more bch() results (side by side). Ignored by the other methods.

format

"text" (default), "markdown", "latex" or "html".

digits

Number of decimal places.

file

Optional path; the table is written there (UTF-8) and returned invisibly.

title, notes

Optional title (caption) and extra notes (character vector); title = NULL uses a default title.

label

LaTeX label (\label{}), LaTeX output only.

what

For a single model: "fit" (default), "parameters", "classes" or "regression".

labels

Optional row labels of the models in a fit comparison, one per model.

lmr, blrt

Optional LMR / BLRT results for a fit comparison: lists with one lmr() / blrt() result (or NULL, e.g. for the one-class model) per model, or numeric vectors of p-values. For LMR the adjusted p-value is shown.

stars

Significance thresholds for one, two and three stars; FALSE for none.

se

Logical; show standard errors (in parentheses in the wide layout).

ci

Logical; show level confidence intervals (Wald, estimate +/- z SE) instead of standard errors.

level

Confidence level.

layout

"wide" (classes as columns, default) or "long" (one row per parameter).

kinds

Character vector of parameter kinds to include (see the kind column of parameters()); default: all, except the logit thresholds of an LCA.

pairwise

Also list the pairwise Wald tests in the notes (BCH, DCAT).

Value

An object of class lm_table_output: a character string that prints as the table (returned invisibly when file is given). In R Markdown / Quarto it is emitted as is. See lm_render().

Details

What is tabulated depends on x:

  • Several models (lm_table(m1, m2, m3) or a list of models): a side-by-side fit comparison with one row per model: K, free parameters, log-likelihood, AIC, BIC, sample-size adjusted BIC, entropy, smallest class (percent), and LMR / BLRT p-values when supplied through lmr / blrt. The lowest AIC, BIC and saBIC are set in bold (markdown, LaTeX, HTML), with a note. Rows are labelled by labels, else by the argument names, else by the argument expressions (expressions longer than 25 characters become "Model i").

  • One model, by what: "fit" (one row of fit statistics), "parameters" (estimates of parameters() with standard errors in parentheses, confidence intervals or neither; layout = "wide" puts classes side by side, "long" gives one row per parameter with z and p; LCA thresholds are omitted unless requested through kinds; probabilities and variances are not starred because tests against zero are not meaningful), "classes" (class proportions, modal counts and average posterior probabilities) or "regression" (one-step latent class regression, coeftable()).

  • Auxiliary results: r3step() (logits, SE or CI, odds ratios, p, one panel per class), bch() (means with SEs; several outcomes side by side when more bch() results are given in ...), dcat() (probabilities with SEs), lmr(), blrt() and compare_models() (two-model and multi-model comparisons).

  • Any data frame, or a table built with lm_tab().

lm_table() is an S3 generic: other packages extend it with methods that build an lm_tab() and pass it to lm_render() (latentclasscausal does this for its causal results). Not every argument applies to every method; the default method stops with an informative error.

See also

lm_tab() and lm_render() to build tables; fittable(), parameters().

Examples

# any data frame
d <- data.frame(K = 1:3, BIC = c(1520.4, 1488.2, 1495.0))
lm_table(d, format = "markdown", title = "Class enumeration")
#> **Class enumeration**
#> 
#> | K | BIC |
#> | :--- | ---: |
#> | 1.000 | 1520.400 |
#> | 2.000 | 1488.200 |
#> | 3.000 | 1495.000 |

data(aces)
# \donttest{
# publication tables for the ACE classes
fits <- lapply(1:5, function(k) lca(aces, starts_with("ace_"), K = k))
#> Starting Julia ...
names(fits) <- paste(1:5, "classes")
lm_table(fits, lmr = lapply(fits, function(m) if (m$info$fit$K > 1) lmr(m)))
#> Model fit
#> ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> Model      K  Par.         LL        AIC        BIC      saBIC  Entropy  Smallest (%)   LMR p
#> ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> 1 classes  1     8  -6197.364  12410.729  12453.234  12427.821        —             —       —
#> 2 classes  2    17  -5413.828  10861.655  10951.980  10897.976    0.781          35.9  <0.001
#> 3 classes  3    26  -5316.153  10684.307  10822.451  10739.856    0.794          18.2  <0.001
#> 4 classes  4    35  -5248.007  10566.015  10751.977  10640.792    0.759           9.9  <0.001
#> 5 classes  5    44  -5240.280  10568.560  10802.342  10662.566    0.771           5.2   0.116
#> ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
#> LL = log-likelihood; Par. = free parameters; saBIC = sample-size adjusted BIC; Smallest = smallest class (estimated proportion).
#> LMR p = Lo-Mendell-Rubin adjusted LRT p-value (K - 1 vs. K classes).
f <- tempfile(fileext = ".tex")
lm_table(fits[[4]], what = "parameters", format = "latex", file = f)
lm_table(fits[[4]], what = "parameters", layout = "long", ci = TRUE)

lm_table(r3step(fits[[4]], aces, c(female, low_parent_edu)), format = "markdown")
#> **Three-step (R3STEP) latent class regression**
#> 
#> | Term | Logit | SE | OR | p |
#> | :--- | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
#> | *Class 1 vs. 4* |  |  |  |  |
#> | (Intercept) | 2.097\*\*\* | 0.192 | 8.143 | <0.001 |
#> | female | -0.020 | 0.216 | 0.981 | 0.928 |
#> | low_parent_edu | -0.769\*\*\* | 0.218 | 0.464 | <0.001 |
#> | *Class 2 vs. 4* |  |  |  |  |
#> | (Intercept) | 0.628\* | 0.245 | 1.875 | 0.010 |
#> | female | 0.125 | 0.272 | 1.133 | 0.645 |
#> | low_parent_edu | -0.118 | 0.272 | 0.889 | 0.666 |
#> | *Class 3 vs. 4* |  |  |  |  |
#> | (Intercept) | 0.441 | 0.260 | 1.554 | 0.090 |
#> | female | -0.195 | 0.293 | 0.822 | 0.505 |
#> | low_parent_edu | 0.187 | 0.298 | 1.206 | 0.530 |
#> 
#> *Multinomial logits against class 4; OR = odds ratio; n = 1500. Robust standard errors.*  
#> *\* p < 0.05; \*\* p < 0.01; \*\*\* p < 0.001*  
lm_table(bch(fits[[4]], aces, depress), bch(fits[[4]], aces, smoker), format = "html")
